cover.title: Design a scalable Food Delivery App
cover.subtitle: Zomato/Swiggy case study
cover.tagline: A three-sided marketplace: customers, restaurants and riders. 50M monthly users, 5M orders/day, ~500 orders/s at peak.

items: A customer orders from a ==nearby restaurant==
A rider delivers it in about **30-40 min**
Three actors: customer app, restaurant tablet/POS, delivery partner app
Time is the product: late food means a lost order
Supply and demand match inside a ==5-8 km== radius
So the system is **sharded** by city and zone
Every extra minute of delay raises ==cancellation rates==
Hence latency is a __product metric__, not just an ops one
Ask who owns the ==food and fleet== first
Fix the delivery radius: **5-8 km**
Name the peak: about 500 orders/s
List what is out of scope before drawing boxes

blocks.title: Open with scope
blocks.text: State in-scope and out-of-scope aloud first; it shapes every later choice.

blocks.title: Summary (Food Delivery App)
blocks.text: A hyperlocal, three-sided marketplace: shard by city and zone, treat latency as a product metric, and judge it by the three targets above.

items: **Customer:** ==search== restaurants, view menu, cart, place order
**Customer:** pay, track, rate, cancel and refund
Requirements say what the app does, not how fast
**Restaurant:** accepts or rejects orders, updates menu and stock
**Rider:** accepts jobs and updates status (picked up, delivered)

blocks.title: Degrade browse first
items: Serve cached lists and stale menus
Pause promos before search
Keep ordering up at 99.95%

blocks.note: peak is about 2x the window average

items: Pings stay ==hot for 7 days==, then archived
3.6 TB/year is **before** replication

blocks.title: Capacity planning
blocks.text: Provision for 3x peak on New Year's Eve and the IPL final.

items: Strong consistency only where money moves
Writes are dominated by 100k rider pings/s
Browse may degrade, ordering may not
Sizing for the daily **average**, not the peak
Forgetting replication in storage totals
Skipping festival days in capacity plans

blocks.title: Estimate with round numbers
blocks.text: State assumptions aloud; the method matters more than exact digits.

blocks.note: use the peak rate for sizing

items: Orders are the **smallest** load but need strict consistency
Pings are the ==largest== write load but tolerate loss
Discovery is read-heavy, so scale it with replicas
Shed promos and recommendations first
Keep search up next
Protect order placement ==last==

blocks.title: Pre-scale the peaks
blocks.text: Scale up before lunch and dinner; autoscale on queue lag for surges.

blocks.title: Read-heavy design
blocks.text: Catalog reads outnumber writes about 100:1, so cache and search replicas dominate.
The ==high-level architecture== splits the app into ten services behind one **edge**. Requests enter through a CDN, an API gateway, then a backend-for-frontend (BFF) per client.

items: Entry path: CDN → API gateway (auth, rate limiting, routing) → BFF
BFF per client: customer app, restaurant tablet, rider app
Services: catalog, search, cart, order, payment, dispatch, tracking, notification, ETA, pricing
Sync calls (gRPC/REST) only on the checkout path
Async events on Kafka for everything downstream
Topics: `order.events`, `payment.events`, `rider.location`
Partition key: `orderId` or `riderId` keeps order per entity
Geo partitioning: shard by ==city==, then by geohash cell
A dispatch query never crosses regions
Database-per-service: share via APIs and events, **never** shared tables

blocks.text: Order, tracking and search scale at very different rates, so each gets its own team and fleet.

blocks.title: Edge protections
items: Rate limit about 10 req/s per user
Bot filtering at the gateway
Idempotency keys on write APIs
Sync chain of 6+ services in checkout: one slow hop multiplies **tail latency**
One shared database for all services: coupling and a single point of failure

blocks.title: 6. Summary
blocks.text: Sync for checkout, Kafka for the rest, one store per service, and shard by city.

items: Store ==restaurants==, menus, items, prices, availability
Store operating hours per restaurant
Scale: 300k restaurants x 100 items = **30M** items
Menu size about 50 KB per restaurant, so about 15 GB total

spec.title: Catalog write path and read path

items: Restaurant edits an item in the dashboard or POS
Catalog DB commits the row
CDC publishes the change to Kafka
Consumers invalidate the Redis menu key
Search reindexes the item
Stock toggles propagate in **under 5 s** via events, not polling

blocks.note: Read hits cache; write emits event

items: Price and stock carry a ==version== on every change
Cart stores the version it saw, per item
At checkout a version mismatch means the item changed
PATCH sets a state, so a retry is safe

rows: Target under 5 s, alert beyond it

items: Reads far outnumber writes, so cache menus in Redis
Serve images from the CDN, never from the DB
Use events for stock, not polling
Never trust the cache alone at checkout
Stock toggle reaches users in **under 5 s**
Price change bumps the item ==version==
POS silent for 3 heartbeats: auto-pause
Writes enter only via the dashboard or ==POS integration==
Reads hit the Redis cache; images come from the CDN
Read:write is about **100:1** on the catalog

blocks.title: Cache is a hint
blocks.text: Serve menus from Redis, but let checkout re-validate every item.

blocks.title: Why events
blocks.text: Events push a stock flip in seconds; polling adds lag and load.

items: Find ==open, deliverable== restaurants and dishes near the user
Rank results well: relevance, distance, ETA, quality
Serve search P99 under **300 ms** at browse-heavy traffic
{icon:elasticsearch} Elasticsearch with a `geo_point` field; filters: cuisine, rating, veg, price, open-now
==Serviceability==: delivery radius must cover the user, usually **5-8 km**
Ranking: distance, ETA, rating, popularity, affinity, promos, kitchen load

blocks.title: Why H3
blocks.text: All 6 neighbors sit at equal distance, so the radius ring is clean.

items: Edge n-gram or ==completion suggester==, P99 under **100 ms**
Typo tolerance: fuzzy match of 1-2 edits
Restaurant doc holds name, cuisine and top-dish tokens
Dish-level search needs a **separate item index**

blocks.note: dishes live in a separate index

items: Offset paging skips or repeats rows as the index changes
Cursor encodes the last sort key plus a doc id

blocks.title: Cursor over offset
blocks.text: Cursor paging stays stable while the index changes under the user.

items: Catalog commit goes through the CDC pipeline to the index in under **10 s**
Availability flips are ==partial updates==, not full reindex
If Elasticsearch is down, serve a **cached top-restaurants list per H3 cell**
Refresh the fallback list per ==H3 cell==
Flip the open flag with a partial update
Zero results: relax filters before the radius
Retry with ==fuzzy match== of 1-2 edits
Relax filters first, then widen the radius
Suggest popular dishes in the same H3 cell
Log each miss to fix the **zero-result rate**

blocks.title: Watch zero results
blocks.text: A rising zero-result rate often means a stale index or a radius bug.

blocks.title: Eventual is fine
blocks.text: Search may lag 10 s; checkout re-validates, so money stays safe.

items: Hold items; ==validate prices and stock==
Apply coupons; compute taxes and fees
Hand off to the {blue:order service}
**One restaurant** per cart; another one prompts a clear
Store: Redis hash by `userId`, 24 h TTL; DB write only on order

blocks.title: 3. Checkout Flow
items: 1) Add item, validate against catalog
2) Reprice, then apply coupon
3) Checkout re-validates the cart
4) Create a ==PENDING== order
5) Then initiate payment

blocks.text: Bill: item total + GST + delivery fee + packaging + platform fee - discounts = ==payable==

blocks.title: 6. Idempotency and Consistency
items: Checkout re-checks price, stock, serviceability, open status
Any drift returns **409** with the new bill
Coupons enforced server-side: user limit, min order, expiry
Global budget: Redis atomic `DECR`

blocks.title: 7. Failure Scenarios
items: Double-tap pay: same key returns the same order
Budget hits 0 mid-checkout: bill recomputed, clear message

blocks.title: 8. Key Metrics
items: Cart-to-order conversion
Checkout P99 under ==1 s==
Price-mismatch rate
Coupon abuse rate

slides.page_title: Order Saga, Outbox and State Machine

items: ==Source of truth== for the whole order lifecycle
**Orchestrate** payment, restaurant, dispatch and notifications
Peak load: about 500 orders/s, strongly consistent writes

blocks.title: 3. State Machine
items: {icon:postgresql} CREATED → PAYMENT_PENDING → PLACED → ACCEPTED
PREPARING → READY → PICKED_UP → ==DELIVERED==; or CANCELLED → REFUNDED
Code validates moves: DELIVERED can **never** return to PREPARING
Each move: `UPDATE ... WHERE status = expected`, 0 rows = reject
No reply in **3 min**: auto-reject, cancel, refund

blocks.title: 4. Data Model
items: `OrderEvent` is append-only: audit trail, easy replay and debug
Shard by `userId` for history; index `restaurantId` for dashboard

blocks.title: 6. Idempotency and Failures
items: Duplicate Kafka event: ==idempotent consumer==, key `(orderId, eventId)`
Crash after payment, before PLACED: **reconciler** scans stuck orders every 1 min
Outbox relay retries, so no event is lost

blocks.title: Say saga + outbox
blocks.text: In interviews, name both: the saga compensates, the outbox never loses an event.

slides.subtitle: (Food Delivery App)

blocks.title: 7. Key Metrics
items: Order success rate above **99%**
Restaurant acceptance rate; cancellation rate
Time per state: P50 and P99
Collect money via ==UPI==, cards, wallets and COD
Handle **refunds** when orders cancel or time out
Run daily ==reconciliation== against gateway reports
Never store raw card data: use a PCI-compliant gateway
Order created, then payment intent created
User pays at the gateway (UPI, card, wallet)
==Webhook== confirms, order moves to **PLACED**
Client redirect is only a hint: also poll gateway status for ==2 min==
Ledger: ==double-entry== rows for customer, platform, restaurant, rider
Rows are **append-only**: corrections are new rows, never updates
One ==idempotency key== per order: no double charge
The gateway enforces the same key again
**Failover**: route UPI to a secondary PSP when primary success rate drops below 95%
Payment success rate **above 97%**
==P99 webhook delay==
Refund turnaround time
Reconciliation mismatch count

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: Pick the best rider: balance ==speed==, cost and fairness
Locations in a Redis geo index or H3 cells, ping every **5 s**
Candidates: within 3 km, free or finishing a drop, by distance
Score: pickup ETA, prep time, rating, acceptance, load, heading
Start when kitchen is ~**8 min** from ready, so rider arrives with food
Offer to top rider with a **15 s** timeout
On reject or timeout, go to the next candidate
Batching: 1 rider, 2 orders, nearby restaurants and customers

blocks.title: Dispatch early, not late
blocks.text: Assign at ~8 min before ready: too early idles the rider, too late cools the food.

blocks.title: 6. Key Metrics
items: Assignment time P50 under **20 s**
Rider acceptance rate
Rider idle time
Orders per rider per hour

blocks.title: Why batch
blocks.text: Waiting 10-30 s lets the solver pair riders and orders better than first-come greedy.

items: Reassign keeps the same ==orderId==
Offer expiry frees the rider at once
Each retry is logged on `Assignment`
No riders: widen radius in steps, add incentive or show **longer ETA**
Rider offline after accept: **60 s** heartbeat loss triggers reassignment
Double accept: conditional update on offer status, one winner

blocks.title: Fail soft
blocks.text: A longer honest ETA beats a cancelled order with cold food.

items: Ingest rider **location pings**, show ==live map== with smooth ETA
Peak ==100k pings/s== × ~100 B ≈ 10 MB/s
Ping = `(riderId, lat, lng, speed, ts, battery)`
Adaptive rate: 5 s moving, 30 s idle; saves battery, ~40% less traffic
Customer opens map; WebSocket maps to ==orderId==
Location service publishes to that order's channel
Push every 3-5 s; poll fallback on poor networks
==Map matching== snaps GPS to roads; Kalman filter smooths jitter

blocks.note: POST is batched; GET is the fallback

blocks.title: ☆ 6. Failure Scenarios
items: Rider offline: buffer pings, upload batch on reconnect
Server orders buffered pings by `ts`, not arrival
WS node dies: reconnect with ==backoff + jitter==
Lands on another node; resubscribe by orderId

blocks.title: ☆ 7. Key Metrics
items: End-to-end lag P99 **under 5 s**
Active WebSocket connections
Dropped ping rate; map-match accuracy
==Geo partition== pings by city so load spreads
Adaptive ping rate cuts traffic by ~**40%**
Hot store keeps only the **latest** position
History gets a TTL, then moves to S3
Tell the ==customer==, ==restaurant== and ==rider== about key events
Reach them over push, SMS, email and in-app
Event-driven: consume `order.events`, map each event type to a template and a recipient list

blocks.title: Volume estimate
blocks.text: 8 notifications/order x 5M orders = 40M/day. That is about 460/s average and about 2k/s at peak.

blocks.title: 4. Priority, Retry, Fallback
items: High priority: OTP and 'order accepted'
Low priority: promos, **rate-capped** per user
Retry with exponential backoff, then a dead-letter queue (DLQ)
Push fails: critical messages fall back to SMS

blocks.title: 7. Idempotency
items: Dedupe key `(orderId, eventType)`
A replayed event never sends 'delivered' twice

blocks.title: 8. Failure Scenarios
items: Provider outage trips a ==circuit breaker==
Traffic switches to a **backup SMS vendor**
Failed sends retry, then land in the DLQ

blocks.title: Respect preferences
blocks.text: Check opt-in and quiet hours before sending; never rate-cap OTPs.

items: Retry with ==exponential backoff==, then the DLQ
Push fails: critical messages fall back to **SMS**
Provider outage trips a circuit breaker

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: Promise an ==accurate delivery time== at browse, cart and tracking
Balance rider ==supply and demand== through the delivery fee
ETA = ==prep== + rider pickup travel + wait + drop travel
Prep: gradient boosted trees per restaurant, hour, item count
Travel: road graph + live traffic + hourly speed profile
Features: distance, weather, kitchen load, zone riders, weekday, **festival** flag
Shown at browse, cart, tracking; redone on each state change and every **60 s**

blocks.title: 4. Surge and Fairness
items: Zone multiplier = demand / supply over last ==5 min==
Example: 30 orders vs 20 riders gives 1.5x
Capped at about **2x**
Fee shown before payment; quoted fee locked on the cart

blocks.title: 6. Failure: Model Down
items: Fall back to a **rule-based** ETA
Static prep + distance / 20 kmph
Example: 10 min + 4 km / 20 = 22 min

blocks.title: 7. Key Metrics
items: ETA error ==MAPE== under 15%
Orders late by over 10 min: share
Surge-zone coverage
Fee-driven drop-off rate

blocks.title: Why lock the fee
blocks.text: Surge can move in 5 min, so the cart quote is frozen and checkout never changes it.

caption.text:
“How would you design Swiggy for millions of orders?” 🍔📱

This is the system design question that shows up in interviews again and again, so here's the whole thing in handwritten notes. Swipe through 👉

What's covered, in order:

📌 Problem statement and scope
📊 Requirements and scale estimates
🏗️ High-level architecture
🍽️ Restaurant menu and catalog service
🔍 Restaurant discovery and search
🛒 Cart and checkout
📦 Order service and state machine
💳 Payments and refunds
🛵 Delivery partner assignment
📍 Real-time order tracking
🔔 Notifications and communication
⏱️ ETA prediction and dynamic pricing
⚖️ Scaling, failure handling, trade-offs and interview questions
